title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether a Case Shall Be Accepted as an Appeal Case Where a Party Has Indicated an Appeal but Fails to Submit the Appeal Petition Within the Statutory Time Limit

articles.content_en: Where a party indicates an intent to appeal within the statutory appeal period but does not submit an appeal petition, the original trial People's Court shall inform the party that it must, within the statutory period, submit an appeal petition and copies in accordance with the requirements of Article 146 and Article 147, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation).

Where a party, while indicating an appeal within the statutory appeal period, also requests an extension for submitting the appeal petition, the People's Court may, upon review and finding the reason justified, appropriately grant a suitable extension.

Where a party, within the statutory appeal period, only indicates an appeal but neither submits an appeal petition nor requests an extension; or requests an extension but is not granted by the People's Court and fails to submit an appeal petition within the statutory appeal period; or, having been granted an extension, still fails to submit an appeal petition within the extended period, the original judgment or ruling shall become legally effective immediately upon the expiration of the statutory appeal period or the permitted extension period. Where a party disagrees with such judgment or ruling, the People's Court shall handle the matter as a petition and shall not accept it as an appeal case.
August 21, 1989
